en: One who hangs, or causes to be hanged; a hangman, paper hanger, etc.
A person who attempts suicide by hanging.

hanger.ety: Inherited from Middle English hanger, haunger, hangere, equivalent to hang + -er. Cognate with West Frisian hinger (“hanger”), Dutch hanger (“hanger”), German Hänger (“hanger”), Henker (“hangman”), Danish hænger (“hanger”), Norwegian henger (“hanger”), Swedish hängare (“hanger”).

An utterance or sound of the voice like "hem", often indicative of hesitation or doubt, sometimes used to call attention.
To make the sound expressed by the word hem; to hesitate in speaking.

hem.ety: A sound uttered in imitation of clearing the throat (onomatopoeia)

ex.ja: えっへんと大いばりでアリスは胸を張った。

A goalscorer; someone who scores goals.
The chores of maintaining a house as a residence, especially cleaning.
Those workers of an establishment who maintain a house through cleaning, etc.
The act or process of infiltrating, as of water into a porous substance, or of a fluid into the cells of an organ or part of the body.
process by which water on the ground surface enters the soil.

infiltration.ety: From Middle English infiltracioun, from Medieval Latin infiltrātiōnem, infiltrātiō. By surface analysis, infiltrat(e) + -ion.

A language characteristic of a particular group.
To utter jargon; to emit confused or unintelligible sounds.

jargon.ety: From Middle English jargoun, jargon, from Old French jargon, a variant of gargon, gargun (“chatter; talk; language”).

To use a kayak, to travel or race in a kayak.
To traverse (a body of water) by kayak.

kayak.ety: Borrowed from Inuktitut ᖃᔭᖅ (qayaq, “hunter's boat”) (Inuvialuktun), from Proto-Eskimo *qayaʁ. Compare Greenlandic qajaq and Yup'ik qayaq.

ex.en: I came here so that I could go kayaking.
ex.ja: カヤックを乗りにここに来たんだ。

ex.en: I came here to go kayaking.
ex.ja: カヤックを乗りにここに来たんだ。

en: In the International System of Units, the base unit of mass; conceived of as the mass of one litre of water, but now defined by taking th…
The unit of weight such that a one-kilogram mass is also a one-kilogram weight.

kilogram.ety: Borrowed from French kilogramme. By surface analysis, kilo- + gram.

ex.en: How many kilograms did Tom lose last summer?
ex.ja: トムって、去年の夏は何キロ痩せたの？

ex.en: I've gained over two kilograms since coming here.
ex.ja: ここに来てから2キロ以上太っちゃった。

ex.en: I have put on two kilograms this summer.
ex.ja: この夏は2キロ太った。

en: To rest on one's bent knees, sometimes only one; to move to such a position.
To sink down so that the entrance is level with the pavement, making it easier for passengers to enter.

kneel.ety: From Middle English knelen, from Old English cnēowlian (“to kneel”), equivalent to knee + -le. Cognate with Dutch knielen, Low German knelen, dialectal German knielen, Alemannic German chnüle, Danish knæle, all meaning “to kneel”.

ex.en: She knelt down as she came into the church.
ex.ja: 彼女は教会に入ると、ひざまずいた。

ex.en: We all knelt down to pray.

ex.en: We knelt down to pray.
ex.ja: 私たちは跪いて祈った。

One hundred thousand rupees.
Often in the plural: an indefinitely large number; a zillion.

The amount lost due to a leak.

en: Often followed by from: to allow or cause (someone or something) to be free; to set free, to release.
To free (someone or something) from discriminatory or oppressive attitudes, inhibition, or restraint.
A writ issued out of the Chancery to authorize the Exchequer to pay a debt, pension, etc., on behalf of the Crown.
A writ issued to a jailer to release a prisoner on bail.

liberate.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin līberātus (“freed, liberated; absolved, acquitted; released”); see English -ate (suffix forming verbs, and used as the ending of participial adjectives and obsolete past participles from Latin). Līberātus is the perfect passive participle of līberō (“to free, liberate; to absolve, acquit; to release”), from līber (“free, unrestricted”), + -ō (suffix forming regular first-conjugation verbs); and līberō is ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₁léwdʰeros (“free”), from *h₁lewdʰ- (“to grow; people”) + *-teros (contrastive or oppositional adjectival suffix) (*h₁léwdʰer

ex.en: I wish I could go to school naked. It'd be so liberating.
ex.ja: 裸で学校に行けたらいいなぁ、すっごく快適だろうね！

note.ja: liber（自由な）+ ate。自由にする →「解放する」。

en: A slit in a castle wall; today, any similar window for shooting a ranged weapon or letting in light.
A method of escape, especially an ambiguity or exception in a rule or law that can be exploited in order to avoid its effect.
To prepare a building for defense by preparing slits or holes through which to fire on attackers
To exploit (a law, etc.) by means of loopholes.

loophole.ety: From Middle English loupe (“opening in a wall”) + hole, from a Germanic source. By surface analysis, loop + hole. Compare Medieval Latin loupa, lobia and Middle Dutch lupen (“to watch”).

ex.en: The new tax law is full of loopholes.
ex.ja: 新しい税法は抜け穴だらけです。

ex.en: A loophole in the law allowed him to escape prosecution.
ex.ja: 法律に抜け穴があるために彼は起訴を逃れることができた。

A member of the indigenous people of the Cook Islands.
Of, from, or pertaining to the Māori.

Maori.ety: Borrowed from Māori māori (“aborigine, native; normal, ordinary, plain”). Doublet of Maoli.

en: Any species of game fish belonging to either of the genera Tetrapturus or Makaira, with a crested dorsal fin and a pointed, spear-like pr…

marlin.ety: A contraction of marlinspike, named so because of its pointed snout.

en: An expert on mathematics; someone who studies mathematics.

mathematician.ety: From Middle English mathematicion, from Middle French mathematicien, from mathematique f sg (“mathematics”) (from Latin mathēmatica, feminine of mathēmaticus, from Ancient Greek μαθηματικός (mathēmatikós, “fond of learning”), from μάθημα (máthēma, “knowledge, learning”) + -ικός (-ikós)) + Middle French -ien (from Latin -iānus). Displaced native Old English rīmcræftiga. By surface analysis, mathematic + -ian.

ex.en: Young as he is, he is as great a mathematician as ever lived.
ex.ja: 若いけれども彼はこれまでに例のないほどの偉大な数学者である。

ex.en: J. Kepler, astronomer and mathematician, made a study of planets and their movements.
ex.ja: 天文学者で数学者であった、J.ケプラーは、惑星とその運動についての研究をした。

en: A dressing made from vegetable oil, raw egg yolks, vinegar or lemon juice, and seasoning, used on salads, with French fries, in sandwiche…
Any cold dish with that dressing as an ingredient.
To cover or season with mayonnaise.

mayonnaise.ety: Unadapted borrowing from French mayonnaise, possibly named after the city of Maó (Mahón in Spanish), Minorca, whence the recipe was brought back to France. Compare Spanish mahonesa. Alternative suggested origins include the city of Bayonne (bayonnaise); the Duke of Mayenne and the words manier (“to handle”) in French or moyeu (“eye yolk”) in Old French.

ex.en: There are only food supplements in that mayonnaise!
ex.ja: あのマヨネーズの中、添加物ばっかり！

ex.en: Mayonnaise and sesame paste go really well together.
ex.ja: マヨネーズと胡麻ペーストの相性は抜群だ。

ex.en: I have to buy mayonnaise and soy sauce.
ex.ja: マヨネーズと醤油を買わなきゃ。

en: Characterized by very precise, conscientious attention to details.

meticulous.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin meticulōsus (“full of fear, timid, fearful, terrible, frightful”), from metus (“fear”) and -culōsus, extracted from perīculōsus (“perilous”). Sense of “characterized by very precise, conscientious attention to details” is a semantic loan from French méticuleux.

ex.en: It is not necessary to be meticulous.
ex.ja: こせこせする必要はない。

ex.en: He's not a very meticulous guy.
ex.ja: あいつもアバウトな性格だよな。

en: The quality of being modest; having a limited and not overly high opinion of oneself and one's abilities.
Moderate behaviour; reserve.

modesty.ety: Borrowed from Middle French modestie, from Latin modestia; equivalent to modest + -y.

ex.en: This is no time for modesty.
ex.ja: 謙遜している場合じゃないよ。

ex.en: Modesty is befitting to a young girl.
ex.ja: 若い娘には慎みが似つかわしい。

ex.en: Even when one is being praised, modesty is important.
ex.ja: 褒められても謙虚さが大事。

en: A growth of facial hair between the nose and the upper lip.
A curly bracket, { or }.

moustache.ety: Used in English since the 16th century. From Middle French moustache from Italian mostaccio, from Early Medieval Latin mustācium, from Medieval Greek μουστάκιον (moustákion), diminutive of (Doric) Ancient Greek μύσταξ (mústax, “upper lip”), of unknown origin (probably a Pre-Greek substrate). Replaced native English kemp (“moustache”), from Old English cenep.

ex.en: Tom is growing a mustache.
ex.ja: トムは口髭を伸ばしている。

ex.en: Tom grew a mustache.
ex.ja: トムは口ひげを生やした。

ex.en: Tom grew a moustache.
ex.ja: トムは口ひげを生やした。

en: Of a person, creature, group, or species, primarily active during the night.
Of an occurrence, taking place at night, nightly.
A person or creature that is active at night.
A device for telling the time at night, rather like a sundial but read according to the stars.

nocturnal.ety: From Middle French nocturnal, from Late Latin nocturnālis (“nocturnal”), from Latin nocturnus (“nocturnal”), from Latin nox (“night”), from Proto-Indo-European *nókʷts (“night”). Cognates include Ancient Greek νύξ (núx), Sanskrit नक्ति (nákti), Old English niht (English night) and Proto-Slavic *noťь.

ex.en: Some animals are nocturnal.
ex.ja: 夜に活動する動物もいる。

en: A short tube, usually tapering, forming the vent of a hose or pipe.
A short outlet or inlet pipe projecting from the end or side of a hollow vessel, as a steam-engine cylinder or a steam boiler.

nozzle.ety:
From Middle English noselle, equivalent to nose + -le (diminutive suffix).
Compare typologically Russian сопло (soplo) (<~ сопе́ть (sopétʹ), whence also сопа́тка (sopátka)).

en: In an illegal position ahead of the ball, puck, etc.
To the side of the road, past the curb and sidewalk.
An offside play.
The side of a road vehicle furthest from the kerb: the right side if one drives on the left of the road.

offside.ety: From off- + side. Compare German Abseite (“remote area, backside”), German abseits (“out of the way, apart, aside”, adverb), Dutch afzijdig (“neutral, impartial”).

ex.en: An offside... No! We did it!
ex.ja: オフサイド・・・じゃない！やったー！

en: A secret rite or ceremony, typically involving riotous and dissolute behavior, including dancing, drunkenness and indiscriminate sexual a…
A gathering of people to engage in group sex.

orgy.ety: Originally in plural from French orgies, from Latin orgia, from Ancient Greek ὄργια (órgia, “secret rites, mysteries”).

ex.en: During the orgy Megumi ran naked round the lawn.
ex.ja: 乱交パーティーの中で、めぐみはすっぱだかで芝生を走り回った。

en: To lay, spread, or apply (something) over or across (something else); to overspread.
To overwhelm; to press excessively upon.
An image to be overlaid on another; a superimposition or diapositive.
A piece of paper pasted upon the tympan sheet to improve the impression by making it stronger at a particular place.

overlay.ety: From Middle English overleyen, from Old English oferleċġan, from Proto-West Germanic *obarlaggjan, from Proto-Germanic *uberlagjaną, equivalent to over- + lay. Cognate with Saterland Frisian uurläze, úurlääse, Dutch overleggen, German Low German overleggen, överleggen, German überlegen, Swedish överlägga, Norwegian overlegge. Compare overlie.

en: So appalling or sad that one feels or should feel sorry for it; eliciting pity.
Eliciting contempt.

pitiful.ety: From Middle English pityful, piteful, piteeful. By surface analysis, pit(i) + -ful.

ex.en: The pitiful sight moved us to tears.
ex.ja: 気の毒な光景は私たちの涙をさそった。

ex.en: He's unlucky to a pitiful extent.
ex.ja: 彼は気の毒な程不運だ。

ex.en: The pitiful tale fetched tears from the girl.
ex.ja: その哀れな話を聞いて少女は涙を浮かべた。

en: An excessive amount or number; an abundance.
Excess of blood in the skin, especially in the face and especially chronically.

plethora.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin plēthōra, from Ancient Greek πληθώρα (plēthṓra, “fullness, satiety”), from πλήθω (plḗthō, “to be full”) + -η (-ē, nominal suffix).

ex.en: There is a plethora of adverbs of frequency in my language.
ex.ja: 私の言語は頻度を表す副詞の種類が豊富です。

A course or topic that must be completed before another course or topic can be started.

psychosis.ety: From psych- + -osis. Not descended from Ancient Greek ψύχωσις (psúkhōsis, “animation, principle of life”), which is a piecewise cognate.

en: An infectious disease caused by species of Lyssavirus that causes acute encephalitis in warm-blooded animals and people, characterised by…

rabies.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin rabiēs (“rage, madness, fury”). Doublet of rage.

en: A portion of some limited resource, especially food, allocated to a person, group or period.
To supply with a ration; to limit (someone) to a specific allowance of something.
To portion out (especially during a shortage of supply); to limit access to.

ration.ety: From French ration. Doublet of reason and ratio.

ex.en: The government rationed meat during the war.
ex.ja: 戦時中政府は肉を配給にした。

ex.en: We have used our ration of coal for the week.
ex.ja: 一週間分の石炭を使ってしまった。

ex.en: They bargained additional rations of bread and milk.
ex.ja: 彼らはパンと牛乳の追加配給を交渉で決めた。

note.ja: ラテン語 ratio（計算）から。計算して割り当てた量 →「配給（量）・配給する」。rate、ratio と同じ。

en: Narration, account, description, rendering.
To tell; narrate; to relate in detail.

recount.ety: From Old Northern French and Anglo-Norman recunter, variant of Old French reconter.

ex.en: He recounted his unusual experiences.
ex.ja: 彼は奇怪な体験を詳しく話した。

ex.en: Island folklore still recounts the story of the raft.
ex.ja: 島の民間伝承はいまだにそのいかだの話を伝えている。

en: Any quadrilateral having opposing sides parallel and four right angles.
Such a quadrilateral that is oblong (longer than it is wide): one that is not regular (equilateral), that is, any except a square.

rectangle.ety: Borrowed from Middle French, from Old French, from Medieval Latin or Late Latin rectangulum (“right angle”), from Latin rectus (“right”) + angulus (“an angle”).

ex.en: The opposite sides of a rectangle are parallel.
ex.ja: 長方形の対辺は平行である。

ex.en: We encounter similar difficulties when we substitute rectangles for triangles in this configuration.
ex.ja: この構成において、三角形の代わりに長方形を用いても類似の困難が生ずる。

en: Recurring; happening time after time.
Non-transient.

recurrent.ety: From Latin recurrens, present participle of recurrere. Morphologically recur + -ent.

note.ja: re（再び）+ cur（走る）+ rent。再び走ってくる →「繰り返し起こる・再発する」。

en: An additional helping of food or drink at reduced cost.
Refuelling, fuel to refill an empty fuel tank (of a vehicle or machine) or other fuel container.
To fill up once again.
To repeat a prescription.

refill.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Italic *wre-
Latin re-der.
Old French re-bor.
Middle English re-
English re-
English fill
English refill
From re- (“again”) + fill (noun).

ex.en: This refill lasts half a year.
ex.ja: この替え芯は半年持つ。

en: Essential, indispensable, required.
An indispensable item; a requirement.

requisite.ety: From Latin requīsītus, perfect passive participle of requīrō (“to require, seek, ask for”), from which English require.

note.ja: re（再び）+ quis（求める）+ ite。必要として求められる →「必要な（もの）・必須条件」。

en: To wind (something) again.
To wind back, of something clocklike or recordlike, like a cassette, tape, film; especially to then replay or relive.
The act of rewinding.
A button or other mechanism for rewinding.

rewind.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Italic *wre-
Latin re-der.
Old French re-bor.
Middle English re-
English re-
Middle English wynden
English wind
English rewind
From re- + wind.

en: To beguile or lure (someone) away from duty, accepted principles, or proper conduct; to lead astray.
To entice or induce (someone) to engage in a sexual relationship.

seduce.ety: Borrowed from Latin sēdūcō (“to lead apart or astray”), from sē- (“aside, away, astray”) + dūcō (“to lead”); see duct. Compare adduce, conduce, deduce, etc. and Middle English seduct.

ex.en: I tried in vain to seduce her.
ex.ja: 彼女を誘惑しようとしたがむだだった。

ex.en: He seduced her with false promises.
ex.ja: 彼はでたらめな約束をして彼女を誘惑した。

ex.en: This guy is quick in seducing women so you better beware.
ex.ja: あの男は手が早いから気をつけた方がいいよ。

en: To avoid, especially persistently; ostracize.
To escape (a threatening evil, an unwelcome task etc).

shun.ety:
From Middle English schonen (“to decline to do, avoid, fear”), from Old English sċunian (“to shun, fear, avoid”), of uncertain origin, though probably ultimately connected to the Proto-Indo-European root *(s)kewH- (“to cover, conceal”) via Proto-Germanic *skunōną; see that entry for more discussion.
Compare hide, shy, and Sanskrit स्कुनाति (skunāti, “to cover”).

ex.en: He's completely shunned. I'm surprised he's still working here.
ex.ja: あんな四面楚歌の状態で、彼よく仕事してられるよな。

ex.en: Shun will take over my job while I'm away.
ex.ja: 私が不在の間は俊が私の仕事を引き継ぎます。

en: An assistant to another person, especially to a superior or more important person.
In literature, theatre, etc., a good foil of the protagonist, a character who helps emphasize the traits of the main character.

sidekick.ety: From side + kick, which in the late 19th and early 20th century was a slang term for the front side pocket of a pair of trousers, known as the pocket safest from theft. Thus, by analogy, a "side-kick" was a person's closest companion.

en: UK and Australia standard spelling of specter.

ex.en: A spectre is haunting Europe — the spectre of communism.
ex.ja: 一匹の妖怪がヨーロッパを徘徊している。共産主義という妖怪が。

en: Specifically, one that is uncastrated.
A male horse kept primarily as a stud.

stallion.ety: From Middle English stalion, from Middle French estalon (whence modern French étalon), of Germanic origin, akin to stall. Displaced native Old English henġest.

en: The husband of one's biological mother after her initial marriage to or relationship with one's biological father.
The husband of one's parent distinct from one's biological father or person with a similar relationship.

stepfather.ety:
From Middle English stepfader, from Old English stēopfæder, from Proto-Germanic *steupafadēr (“stepfather”), equivalent to step- + father.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian Stäiffoar (“stepfather”), Dutch stiefvader (“stepfather”), German Low German Steevvader (“stepfather”), German Stiefvater (“stepfather”), Swedish styvfar (“stepfather”), Icelandic stjúpfaðir (“stepfather”).

ex.en: My stepfather treats me better than my real father did.
ex.ja: 継父は、実父より良くしてくれます。

en: To kill someone by squeezing the throat so as to cut off the oxygen supply.
To choke, suffocate or throttle, whether the victim survives or not.
A trading strategy using options, constructed through taking equal positions in a put and a call with different strike prices, such that …
